generalProcedure.summary: Italian Dottorato di Ricerca (PhD) admissions for cycle XLII (A.Y. 2026/2027) are competitive public selections (concorso). Most Lazio and Southern universities published calls between May and August 2026; many main deadlines have already closed by early September 2026, with a minority of late windows still open (e.g. Cagliari to 28 Sep 2026; Calabria to 21 Sep 2026; Foggia/Sassari chemistry around 8 Sep 2026). Applications are almost always online via PICA (pica.cineca.it/<slug>/...), Esse3/student portals, or university-specific systems (Infostud, Delphi, GOMP, Roma Tre apps). Standard requirements: second-cycle degree (Laurea Magistrale/Specialistica or equivalent foreign EQF-7) by a call-specific date (often 31 Oct 2026); ID; CV; degree certificate/transcript (IT/EN); often a research project; application fee via PagoPA (typically €20–€35). Selection is usually evaluation of qualifications ± research project + oral interview; English proficiency is commonly assessed at interview and many STEM/social-science boards allow interviews/thesis in English. Scholarships (borsa) follow MUR decree amounts (~€16,243 gross/year) with possible 50% increase for approved research abroad; funded and unfunded seats are listed per programme annex.
generalProcedure.typicalNationalStipend: €16,243 gross/year (DM 247/2022), subject to INPS separate management contributions
generalProcedure.notes: English-taught Italian PhDs are rarely labelled as fully English degree programmes; more often research, seminars, and interviews can be conducted in English. Prefer English-named programmes and annexes that explicitly allow English. Always re-check the official bando/annex for the chosen course before applying. Non-EU winners typically need Universitaly pre-enrolment and a postgraduate study visa.
